sentences.text: This ancient marine reptile measured approximately 1.6 meters in length and possessed a mass exceeding 15 kilograms.
Its skull was remarkably short, accounting for just 6.25 percent of the total body length.
The nasal bones stretched continuously to the very tip of the snout.
The animal featured a short, robust trunk supported by wide, flattened ribs.
An extensive basket of gastralia, or belly ribs, ran along the underside in two parallel rows.
A very long and slender tail, composed of at least 67 vertebrae, lacked a fluke.
Small dermal ossicles, measuring between 2 and 5 millimeters, were located on the neck region.
The head was exceptionally small relative to the rest of the body, making up only 6.25 percent of the total length.
The tail was unusually long and slender, constructed from at least 67 individual vertebrae without a fluke.
Tiny bony plates, ranging from 2 to 5 millimeters in size, covered the neck area.
Remains of this creature were unearthed in central Anhui Province, China.
Scientists know of Sclerocormus from a single, mostly complete fossil specimen.
This specific fossil offers significant insight into the early evolution of ichthyosaurs.
Currently, the Paleobiology Database records only one occurrence of this species.
